paper.title: Retrieval as Reasoning: Self-Evolving Agent-Native Retrieval via LLM-Wiki
paper.central_claim: An agent-native linked Wiki and persistent Error Book improve compositional retrieval and reduce recurring compilation errors by retained constraints and two-layer repair.

provenance.notes: Configured invocation identifies sol/gpt-6.1-sol; no independently accessible provider receipt/session identifier. No probing.

sections_read: Full main text and Appendices A–H, all tables/algorithm/cases

evidence.quote: The Error Book improves the Wiki over time by injecting learned constraints into future compilation prompts and repairing existing errors.
evidence.support_explanation: Retained compiler instructions and Wiki repair from execution validation; within harness RSI scope, not merely query-time reasoning.

evidence.quote: All open constraint rules are appended to the Step 2 compilation prompt, guiding the LLM to avoid known error patterns in subsequent batches.
evidence.support_explanation: Durable YAML rules read by later compilation batches; not trained weights.

evidence.quote: If the error no longer appears after constraint injection, the error entry is marked as closed.
evidence.support_explanation: Closure signal is validator disappearance, not independently measured QA or regression-free edit acceptance.
Bounded final iterative repair, with no demonstrated per-edit rollback or untouched acceptance set.

evidence.quote: we use the first 500 QA examples in the original dataset order. The source corpus for each benchmark is the union of the context paragraphs associated with those 500 examples, and the same corpus is used for all methods.
evidence.support_explanation: Dataset-provided context retrieval, not open-domain Wikipedia; fixed corpus parity.

evidence.quote: Our evaluation compares end-to-end retrieval systems rather than equalizing every retrieval component. LLM-Wiki uses a larger query-time tool-call budget
evidence.support_explanation: Authors explicitly disclose unequal retrieval budget; impacts causality/cost, not metric validity.

evidence.quote: This variant uses the same Wiki compilation and traversal pipeline but disables Error Book updates, constraint injection, and repair.
evidence.support_explanation: Artifact-side ablation groups constraint learning and ordinary repairs together; no separation of learned-rule utility from repair compute.

evidence.quote: The 3.4–4.0 F1-point drop suggests that the Error Book improves downstream retrieval by reducing the impact of recurring structural and semantic construction errors.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported retained-structure QA benefit, not standalone improved-improver proof.

evidence.quote: We sample 240 responses, stratified to cover 3 representative methods
evidence.support_explanation: Human audit denominator and model-comparator coverage.

evidence.quote: Three authors independently annotate each response using the same 0–3 answer-correctness rubric as the GPT-4o-mini judge.
evidence.support_explanation: Human metric check; not independent external reproduction.

evidence.quote: Annotators are blind to both the method identity and the GPT-4o-mini judgment.
evidence.support_explanation: Method-blind, judge-blind manual audit supports measurement credibility.

evidence.locator: Appendix G, Generalization Across Answer LLMs
evidence.quote: we evaluate GPT-4o as an alternative answer LLM while keeping the compiled Wiki fixed
evidence.support_explanation: Direct retained Wiki transfer across consumers, not transfer of learned constraints to unseen corpora.

evidence.quote: making initial construction more expensive than chunk-and-embed approaches, though the cost is amortized over later queries.
evidence.support_explanation: Compilation overhead acknowledged but not quantified into a measured break-even ledger.

evidence.quote: Web-scale and frequently changing corpora will require hierarchical indexing, sharding, stale-fact handling, and global directory maintenance.
evidence.support_explanation: Scalability and dynamic stale-fact management untested.

evidence.quote: Each cell denotes the percentage of detected errors of a given type within the corresponding Wiki, so each column sums to approximately 100%.
evidence.support_explanation: Composition of detected errors is not absolute error prevalence or before/after recurrence reduction.

evidence.quote: On Single-doc questions, HippoRAG 2 outperforms LLM-Wiki by 2.3 AC points.
evidence.support_explanation: Negative regime: structured compression can omit local detail.

evidence.quote: the agent reads an average of only 2.5–3.9 pages per query, compared with RAG’s fixed 5 passages
evidence.support_explanation: Query page counts and latency are reported; no equal tokens/indexing cost account.

evidence.quote: whereas the Error Book targets persistent cross-batch error patterns in knowledge construction through constraint accumulation and repair.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors distinguish durable compilation correction from Reflexion/Self-Refine/Self-RAG query corrections; original adjacent texts not checked.
Exact table values; MuSiQue vs LightRAG 0.659 is 8.0 points by displayed numbers, not prose 8.1.

gap.author_gap: Flat lookup cannot support agent-planned compositional traversal, and compiled stores lack persistent error correction.
gap.checked_gap: Wiki/tool design and bundle-level Error Book help within context-union benchmarks. Prior iterative retrieval means novelty is not reasoning between retrieval calls per se.

claims.text: Wiki structure plus traversal improves multi-hop QA.
claims.setting: 500 questions per Hotpot/MuSiQue/2Wiki, union of provided contexts
claims.baseline_control: Seven baselines, same answer/indexing model and corpus; structure/traversal removals
claims.selection_vs_test: Index-time sources not QA labels reported; no QA-guided rule selection described
claims.result_denominator: F1 .839/.739/.911; best baseline LightRAG .819/.659/.847. Table-rounded MuSiQue difference8.0 points, prose8.1.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Improved end-to-end systems in small provided-context corpora; not budget-equal mechanism superiority or open-domain SOTA.

claims.text: Persistent Error Book reduces recurring errors and helps QA.
claims.setting: Compilation across batches plus downstream QA
claims.baseline_control: All Error Book updates, constraints and repairs disabled together
claims.result_denominator: F1 loss without bundle3.8/4.0/3.4 points; error table only within-corpus type percentages.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Retained validated Wiki bundle useful; no isolated improved compiler or measured cross-batch error recurrence effect.

claims.text: Benefit generalizes to structured multi-document QA and another answer model.
claims.selection_vs_test: Same compiled artifacts reused; separate benchmark compiled independently
claims.result_denominator: AuthTrace All70.4 vs68.3; Single76.0 vs78.3. Human audited240; fixedWiki GPT gains5.1/10.5/16.9 F1 vs Dense.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Some consumer and QA-type robustness, with single-document regression; not universal transfer.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Persistently corrected compiled Wikis improve later QA and transfer to a second answer model in supplied-context corpora. Error-Book bundle ablation supports retained artifact utility, not isolated learned-improver or cross-corpus error-reduction claims.
unresolved: Absolute error recurrence and semantic-checker accuracy

G.reason: Concrete source-organization/agent-traversal and recurring-compilation-error gap; strong graph/tree neighbors and iterative retrieval acknowledged. Broad first-retrieval-as-reasoning claim exceeds checked novelty boundary.

M.reason: Error→root cause→YAML constraint→future compile plus structural/semantic repairs connects mechanism to source-grounding failures. Constraint quality/closure and repair interaction lack a regression-safe selector.

X.reason: Persisted artifact, tools and bounded repair pseudo-code reconstruct core path. Source-grounded semantic checker thresholds, closed-rule continued reuse, no-regression gate and stale-fact retirement remain underspecified.

E.measurement.reason: Standard F1/EM and gold-claim judged AC are checked by 240 method-blind human responses (89.6% agreement, kappa .79). Semantic-validator accuracy itself not externally audited.

E.causality.reason: Structure/traversal/Error-Book ablations with same base model/corpus and fixed-Wiki reader transfer support real effects. More tool budget and grouped all-Error-Book removal leave simple repair-vs-learning attribution unresolved.

E.holdout.reason: Source-only compilation and validator feedback, not reported QA-label optimization; later QA and alternative frozen reader show retained benefit. First500 context-union setting and no held-out ingestion transfer limit broader claims.

E.statistics.reason: 500 questions each, 240 audited outputs and mixed single-document result are given. Full main text and Appendices A–H have no main QA intervals, compilation seeds or recurrence-rate denominators. Human agreement is metric validation, not system-run variance.

E.cost.reason: Query latency and average pages supplied; acknowledged larger query budget and unpriced compilation/repair/judge costs leave total-cost efficiency and amortization unverified.

reason: Complete fixed-version material sufficient for scoped system review; Error Book supplies durable feedback-driven harness changes.
rationale: 持久错误约束和修复后的Wiki确有后续QA收益；尚未分离约束学习与额外修复预算，动态大库、成本及跨运行统计证据不足。
